currentContext.strengths: Indigenous digital mapping and navigation built specifically for India's needs, reflected in growing consumer trust and adoption|Deep-tech positioning with AI-led capabilities embedded across products, platforms and internal processes long before AI became a mainstream theme|Scale of the Mappls consumer platform — cumulative reach of more than 45 million users after adding over 10 million downloads and pre-installations during the year|Strong revenue visibility from an executable order book and pipeline exceeding Rs 1,750 crore entering FY2026-27, built on strategic wins across Automotive OEMs, Enterprise, Government, Logistics and Mobility|Long-standing partnerships with government agencies, public institutions, enterprises and developers reinforcing its position as a trusted partner in India's digital infrastructure journey|Healthy profitability profile — EBITDA margins of approximately 37% maintained through disciplined cost management and prudent capital allocation|Full control over the IoT/Gtropy business following buyout of founding stakeholders, enabling greater operational and strategic alignment across the Group|Founder-led board with promoter executives and a nine-member board of which five are independent directors
currentContext.strategies: Enter a new phase of accelerated, platform-led growth built on the integration of Gtropy, expansion of Mappls DT and global ambitions through Terra Link.|Strengthen leadership as India's premier geospatial and location intelligence platform company on a proprietary, full-stack geospatial platform spanning Automotive, Enterprise, Government and IoT verticals.|Scale a SaaS, PaaS and MaaS business model with multiple recurring revenue streams across software, platforms and IoT solutions.|Evolve the IoT-led business into a high-margin, recurring revenue business through software-led monetisation and device ecosystem expansion.|Expand the international footprint through strategic partnerships and subsidiaries, particularly in Southeast Asia (Workmate won its first Southeast Asian client in the Oil & Gas space).|Concentrate technology investment on AI-driven geospatial analytics, Digital Twin and simulation technologies, real-time mapping and navigation systems, and integrated IoT and mobility platforms.|Grow the Map-led business as the cornerstone of growth by expanding across BFSI, e-commerce, logistics, payments and enterprise automation, including the Geo-Verify AI location verification platform powered by proprietary Geo-LLM technology.|Scale the government and public-sector business across defence intelligence systems, property tax digitisation, urban governance, vehicle tracking and emergency response systems, leveraging regulatory alignment and an indigenous data advantage.|Deepen automotive embedded penetration in EV navigation, ADAS/DMS, EV telemetry and connected mobility platforms, and keep strengthening the consumer Mappls app ecosystem.|Continue investments in innovation and technology to sustain the growth trajectory.|The Board recommended a dividend of Rs. 3.50 per equity share (175%) for the financial year ended March 31, 2026, placed for members' approval as an ordinary resolution based on the recommendation of the Audit Committee and the Board. The Company also manages a treasury book: members passed a special resolution at the AGM of 25.07.2025 granting power to manage treasury operations by way of investing and making loans / investing / providing guarantee / security in excess of the limits specified under Section 186 of the Companies Act, 2013, and at the AGM of 09.08.2024 approved increasing the limit for giving guarantee or security in connection with loans availed by material subsidiary Gtropy Systems Private Limited — indicating deployment of surplus into fixed-rate interest-bearing investments (bonds and fixed deposits) and support to subsidiaries. Equity-linked compensation is administered through the Employee Stock Option Plan, 2008, whose modification was approved by special resolution at the AGM of 01.09.2023 and again through postal ballot on 3rd January, 2026.|Certification stack mapped to the NGRBC principles: CMMI ML-5, ISO 14001:2015 (environmental management), ISO 45001:2018 (occupational health & safety), ISO/IEC 27001:2013 and ISO/IEC 20000-1:2018 (information security and IT service management), and ISO 9001:2015 (quality management).|Sole disclosed commitment with a stated goal: a strategic target of ₹1,000 crore in revenue, explicitly with a fluid timeline so the company can 'adapt to evolving market conditions and growth opportunities while maintaining its focus on sustainable value creation'. No environmental or social target with a defined timeline is disclosed.|Materiality assessment: no material responsible business conduct or sustainability issues identified — the BRSR materiality table is 'Nil' on the stated basis that, given the nature of the business, it is not directly applicable.|ESG ownership sits with the Risk Management Committee constituted by the Board on 27 July 2021, tasked with incorporating sustainability into core business decisions and internal operations and with reviewing ESG progress and performance; Group Chairman & MD Rakesh Kumar Verma is the highest authority for BRSR implementation.|Policy architecture: all nine NGRBC principles are covered by Board-approved policies, translated into procedures and extended to value-chain partners; however, no independent external assessment of how those policies work has been carried out, and the Committee/Board review of performance against them is scheduled for FY 2026-27.|Stakeholder grievance redressal mechanisms are in place for every stakeholder group with a published Grievance Redressal Policy for Stakeholders; complaints were Nil from communities, investors, shareholders, employees and value-chain partners, while customer complaint resolution improved to almost 99% from almost 95%.|CSR is applicable to the company under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013.|Board diversity at 33.33% women with zero women among Key Managerial Personnel, and permanent-employee turnover held at 9.39% (from 9.87% and 9.75% in the two prior years).
currentContext.expansion: The routed sections of the FY2025-26 annual report disclose no named capex project, plant, capacity addition, commissioning or ramp-up timeline for C.E. Info Systems (MapmyIndia) - consistent with an asset-light geospatial software and platform business. The only explicit capex reference is in the BRSR, where the Company reports Nil R&D and Nil capital expenditure invested in specific technologies to improve the environmental and social impacts of products and processes, in both FY 2025-2026 and FY 2024-2025, with the details column marked N.A. The BRSR also notes the Company's view that end-of-life product reclamation guidance on plastics, e-waste and hazardous waste is not relevant to its activities because it is a service provider. On structure, a footnote to the related-party investment disclosure identifies PT Terra Link Technologies as a joint venture in which the Company has made an investment, excluded from the related-party investment ratio; no further detail on its scope, geography or build-out is given in the routed text. Expansion language in the MD&A is directed at the demand environment rather than at the Company's own asset base: government-led capex on infrastructure, logistics and urban transformation; expansion of digital public infrastructure including digital identity, payments and geospatial frameworks; increased Union Budget 2025-26 allocation for the Geospatial Mission and digital infrastructure; expansion of the DIGIPIN digital addressing system; Operation Dronagiri and Mission Mausam; and expansion of aftermarket IoT devices, logistics, e-commerce and fintech ecosystems. Management frames the Map-led business as resilient despite temporary moderation in certain geospatial and mapping projects, supported by Mappls MaaS, PaaS and SaaS offerings, embedded automotive navigation, enterprise location intelligence and government digital transformation initiatives, while describing the IoT-led business as delivering exceptional growth in FY26 - platform and product build-out rather than physical capacity being the stated vector of growth. No delivery-centre, office footprint, headcount capacity or acquisition-driven capacity addition is quantified in the routed text.

frameworks.|The National Geospatial Policy is liberalising access to geospatial data, promoting private sector participation and encouraging indigenous development; India's geospatial sector is projected to grow exponentially.|Union Budget 2025-26 raised allocation for the Geospatial Mission and digital infrastructure, expanded Digital Addressing Systems (DIGIPIN), and funded drone/AI initiatives (Operation Dronagiri) and climate and weather intelligence (Mission Mausam).|Automotive shift towards electrification, connectivity and software-defined vehicles is making embedded and fintech ecosystems.|The government sector represents a high-impact, long-term growth opportunity driven by large-scale digital transformation, Atmanirbhar Bharat policy push, higher budgetary allocation for digital infrastructure and adoption of Digital Twin and AI-led governance models.|The IoT segment is evolving into a high-margin, recurring revenue business, aided by a significant increase in high-margin SaaS revenues, which contributed 66% of IoT revenues versus 54.3% in FY25, and by growth in fleet management, telematics, video telematics and aftermarket IoT devices.|Despite temporary moderation in certain geospatial and mapping projects, the Map-led business demonstrated resilience, supported by demand for Mappls MaaS, PaaS and SaaS offerings, embedded automotive visibility, an expanding customer base, increasing adoption of location-based services and continued investment in innovation and technology.|The convergence of geospatial intelligence with AI, IoT and digital platforms is moving the industry from a niche capability to a core digital infrastructure layer.|Stated challenges for the Indian economy: exposure to global demand fluctuations, capital market volatility and commodity price uncertainties, alongside geopolitical realignment and supply chain reconfiguration globally.|The order book expanded significantly during FY26, providing strong visibility for future growth.|Open Order Book increased 17% YoY to Rs 1,754.4 Cr.|Annual new order bookings increased 24% YoY to Rs 785.4 Cr.|Fixed-price contracts increased to Rs 492.2 Cr.|Government business continued to scale with an open order book exceeding Rs 200 Cr, annual billings exceeding Rs 100 Cr and healthy cash collections exceeding Rs 100 Cr.|Strong order book visibility is cited as a key support for sustaining the growth trajectory.

risks.risk: No material ESG/business-conduct risks identified in BRSR — the entire materiality table is returned 'Nil'
risks.note: BRSR Q26 (material responsible business conduct issues, with rationale, mitigation and financial implications) is filled 'Nil' across every column, with the explanation 'Given the nature of the business, this is not directly applicable.' A blank materiality assessment means there is no disclosed register of environmental/social risks, mitigations or financial implications for investors to track year on year.

risks.risk: Government/PSU revenue dependence within the customer mix
risks.note: One of the four stated verticals is Government — central, state and local government organisations, ministries, departments and PSUs — buying geospatial dashboards, GIS health/crime analytics and address-standardisation solutions. Public-sector demand is tender- and budget-cycle driven, making that portion of revenue lumpy and politically/procurement sensitive.

risks.risk: High customer-complaint volume concentrated in the consumer/retail channel
risks.note: 5,984 customer complaints were filed in FY 2025-26 versus 'Nil' from every other stakeholder group (communities, investors, shareholders, employees, value-chain partners). Resolution improved to almost 99% from almost 95%, but the absolute volume shows the Mappls app / Move IoT retail channel carries a service-quality and brand-reputation exposure that the B2B verticals do not.

risks.risk: Execution risk on the ₹1,000 crore revenue goal — an aspiration with no committed timeline
risks.note: The only specific commitment disclosed under BRSR Q5/Q6 is a strategic goal of ₹1,000 crore revenue, and the company twice states 'the timeline for attaining this milestone remains fluid' and 'may evolve based on market conditions, business opportunities, and overall economic factors.' An unbounded target cannot be missed but also cannot be held to account, so the growth roadmap is unverifiable.

risks.risk: Key-person and promoter-family concentration at the top of the structure
risks.note: Co-founders Rakesh Kumar Verma (Group Chairman & MD) and Rashmi Verma (Executive Director, CTO & CHRO) plus Rohan Verma (Joint MD) hold the executive spine; Rakesh Kumar Verma is also named the highest authority for BRSR implementation. The CTO and CHRO roles are combined in one founder, concentrating both technology and people leadership in a single individual.

risks.risk: Talent-retention exposure in a pure-IP, people-dependent map/technology business
risks.note: Permanent-employee turnover ran at 9.39% in FY 2025-26 (9.87% FY 2024-25, 9.75% FY 2023-24) — steady but material for a firm whose asset base is map data and software engineering skill. There are no workers, only employees ('NA' throughout the workers rows), so attrition is the sole labour-side risk channel.

risks.risk: Governance oversight of sustainability is thinly resourced and internally validated only
risks.note: The Risk Management Committee (constituted 27 July 2021) is described as a management-level committee of 4 directors, only half of them Independent, and is chaired by Rohan Verma — described in the same disclosure as a 'Non-Executive Director' while the board list names him Joint Managing Director, an internal inconsistency. Policy review by the Committee and Board is deferred to FY 2026-27, and no external agency has independently assessed the working of the policies.

risks.risk: Diversity concentrated at board level but absent from executive management
risks.note: Women hold 33.33% of Board of Directors seats but 0% of Key Managerial Personnel positions, and female representation is 14.73% of total employees (17.65% of permanent, 11.21% of non-permanent). The gap between board optics and the executive bench is a succession and inclusion watch-item.

one-line thesis: C.E. Info Systems delivered a sharp Q4 inflection (Revenue +54.8% QoQ, EBITDA margin +460bps YoY to 44.6%) driven by the conversion of delayed government and automotive IoT orders, validating the resilience of its INR 1,750 Cr order book despite FY26 full-year stagnation. The strategic pivot toward fixed-price contracts and high-margin IoT SaaS recurring revenue supports a return to >20% growth in FY27, though near-term working capital pressure from government receivables remains a key monitoring metric.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 145 Cr (Q4), INR 474 Cr (FY26, +1% YoY, muted by govt delays); EBITDA: INR 64.7 Cr (Q4), Margin 44.6% (up 460bps YoY); PAT: INR 45.4 Cr (Q4, +171% QoQ), Margin 31.3%; Order Book: INR 1,750 Cr (ex-GST basis ~INR 1,480 Cr), up from INR 1,500 Cr start-of-year; Net Debt: Net Cash ~INR 600 Cr. One-offs: FY26 revenue impacted by ~INR 45-50 Cr deferral of specific automotive IoT and state-level emergency response projects to Q1/Q2 FY27 due to customer regulatory/fleet readiness issues, not execution failure.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Targeting return to >20% CAGR trajectory in FY27 (vs 1% in FY26) backed by INR 1,750 Cr order book; Margin: Steady-state EBITDA >16% (Q4 demonstrated 44.6% potential via operating leverage), IoT margins expanding via SaaS mix; Order Inflow: Robust pipeline across Govt, Auto, Enterprise; Capex: Organic allocation prioritized for IoT hardware deployment (capitalized) and Govt working capital.
order book & pipeline: INR 1,750 Cr open order book (includes 18% GST); FY26 conversion rate ~18% (INR 270 Cr from opening book + INR 200 Cr from new INR 780 Cr bookings); Composition shifting toward fixed-price milestone and minimum-guarantee models improving visibility; Govt segment alone holds >INR 200 Cr.
segment / subsidiary detail: Automotive & Mobility (A&M): +9% FY26, soft Q4 core due to Hyundai variation and delayed IoT fleet rollouts; Consumer & Enterprise (C&E): -3% FY26 due to government deferrals, but +142% QoQ in Q4; Government: Strong recovery in Q4, >INR 200 Cr order book, delayed projects (Energy Response, IoT tenders) pushed to FY27; IoT: Key growth driver, opex model for clients creates fixed asset depreciation on books but high recurring SaaS margins.
growth verticals / optionality: Mappls App ecosystem (45M+ downloads, 10M in FY26) expanding beyond navigation to EV, logistics, and safety; Quick-commerce API integration (e.g., Amazon Now) driving enterprise usage; Digital Twin and Defense tech (AR/VR/GIS) opening large sovereign opportunities; IoT fleet scaling compounding SaaS revenues.
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 EBITDA margin 44.6% driven by operating leverage and favorable mix (higher SaaS/IoT); Full-year FY26 EBITDA margin ~16%; Cost mitigation via value engineering offsetting rising DRAM/NAND prices; Inventory build-up is strategic for demand, not speculative gain.
capex / expansion: INR 120 Cr allocated in FY26 primarily for organic growth: IoT hardware deployment (capitalized as fixed assets, depreciated over 3 years), IP creation, and Govt business working capital; FY27 to continue prioritizing organic capex for IoT fleet expansion.
capital allocation: Cash & equivalents ~INR 600 Cr; Priority 1: Organic growth (IoT hardware, Govt working capital); Priority 2: Strategic small acquisitions; Dividend: Final FY26 dividend INR 3.50/share (175%); Buybacks not explicitly guided but cash position supports flexibility.
risks & watch-items: Government payment cycles elongating DSO (Receivables up to INR 176 Cr from INR 133 Cr), though management cites zero bad debt history; Global semiconductor price inflation impacting IoT hardware costs; Execution timing risk on large fixed-price milestones; Macro strain on government finances potentially delaying future tenders.
management quality / tone: Confident in FY27 recovery citing 'positive inflection point' and 'stronger order pipeline'; Transparent on FY26 misses attributing them strictly to customer-side delays (regulatory/fleet readiness) rather than execution gaps; Emphasized fiscal prudence and clean balance sheet despite rising receivables.
non-obvious takeaways: Reporting segment restructuring planned for FY27 (Auto/Retail, Corporate, Government) to replace confusing A&M/C&E split; Fixed-price contracts now dominate inflows providing better revenue visibility than volume-based models; IoT hardware costs capitalized on balance sheet create temporary asset bloat but drive long-term high-margin recurring revenue streams.

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV. OFSS adds the banking-software annuity, with RPO +17% YoY versus revenue +7% and licence-and-cloud revenue +13% at a 44% operating margin.
themes.driver: Deal/ARR additions; festive digital-payments TPV; merchant-device additions; RBI/regulatory compliance-driven security spend.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company builds intelligent, scalable location and geospatial technology solutions addressing real-world challenges across mobility, governance, enterprise operations, logistics and infrastructure. Its consumer platform Mappls is evolving beyond a navigation application into a comprehensive digital location and mobility ecosystem, with engagement across navigation, logistics, EV experiences, mobility services, safety solutions and geo-intelligence use cases. Alongside maps, the Group operates IoT (Gtropy), Digital Transformation, Defence Technology and Government-facing businesses, and invests across AI, Digital Twins and emerging geospatial technologies.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Automotive & Mobility (A&M): +9% FY26, soft Q4 core due to Hyundai variation and delayed IoT fleet rollouts; Consumer & Enterprise (C&E): -3% FY26 due to government deferrals, but +142% QoQ in Q4; Government: Strong recovery in Q4, >INR 200 Cr order book, delayed projects (Energy Response, IoT tenders) pushed to FY27; IoT: Key growth driver, opex model for clients creates fixed asset depreciation on books but high recurring SaaS margins.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: INR 1,750 Cr open order book (includes 18% GST); FY26 conversion rate ~18% (INR 270 Cr from opening book + INR 200 Cr from new INR 780 Cr bookings); Composition shifting toward fixed-price milestone and minimum-guarantee models improving visibility; Govt segment alone holds >INR 200 Cr.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: Targeting return to >20% CAGR trajectory in FY27 (vs 1% in FY26) backed by INR 1,750 Cr order book; Margin: Steady-state EBITDA >16% (Q4 demonstrated 44.6% potential via operating leverage), IoT margins expanding via SaaS mix; Order Inflow: Robust pipeline across Govt, Auto, Enterprise; Capex: Organic allocation prioritized for IoT hardware deployment (capitalized) and Govt working capital.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Mappls App ecosystem (45M+ downloads, 10M in FY26) expanding beyond navigation to EV, logistics, and safety; Quick-commerce API integration (e.g., Amazon Now) driving enterprise usage; Digital Twin and Defense tech (AR/VR/GIS) opening large sovereign opportunities; IoT fleet scaling compounding SaaS revenues.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India remains one of the fastest-growing major economies, with FY2026 GDP growth expected to remain robust at 6.5%-7.0%, supported by sustained domestic demand and public investment.
- Government-led capex on infrastructure, logistics and urban transformation, plus expansion of Digital Public Infrastructure including digital identity, payments and geospatial frameworks.
- The National Geospatial Policy is liberalising access to geospatial data, promoting private sector participation and encouraging indigenous development; India's geospatial sector is projected to grow exponentially.
- Union Budget 2025-26 raised allocation for the Geospatial Mission and digital infrastructure, expanded Digital Addressing Systems (DIGIPIN), and funded drone/AI initiatives (Operation Dronagiri) and climate and weather intelligence (Mission Mausam).
- Automotive shift towards electrification, connectivity and software-defined vehicles is making embedded navigation and location intelligence standard and raising demand for real-time, high-definition geospatial data; the sector will continue to be a major growth driver for geospatial technologies.
- Enterprise digital transformation is making location intelligence a mission-critical capability, driving sustained demand for scalable geospatial platforms across logistics, e-commerce and fintech ecosystems.
- The government sector represents a high-impact, long-term growth opportunity driven by large-scale digital transformation, Atmanirbhar Bharat policy push, higher budgetary allocation for digital infrastructure and adoption of Digital Twin and AI-led governance models.
- The IoT segment is evolving into a high-margin, recurring revenue business, aided by a significant increase in high-margin SaaS revenues, which contributed 66% of IoT revenues versus 54.3% in FY25, and by growth in fleet management, telematics, video telematics and aftermarket IoT devices.
- Despite temporary moderation in certain geospatial and mapping projects, the Map-led business demonstrated resilience, supported by demand for Mappls MaaS, PaaS and SaaS offerings, embedded automotive navigation, enterprise location intelligence and government digital transformation initiatives.
- Management remains confident of sustaining the growth trajectory, supported by strong order book visibility, an expanding customer base, increasing adoption of location-based services and continued investment in innovation and technology.
- The convergence of geospatial intelligence with AI, IoT and digital platforms is moving the industry from a niche capability to a core digital infrastructure layer.
- Stated challenges for the Indian economy: exposure to global demand fluctuations, capital market volatility and commodity price uncertainties, alongside geopolitical realignment and supply chain reconfiguration globally.
- The order book expanded significantly during FY26, providing strong visibility for future growth.
- Open Order Book increased 17% YoY to Rs 1,754.4 Cr.
- Annual new order bookings increased 24% YoY to Rs 785.4 Cr.
- Fixed-price contracts increased to Rs 492.2 Cr.
- Government business continued to scale with an open order book exceeding Rs 200 Cr, annual billings exceeding Rs 100 Cr and healthy cash collections exceeding Rs 100 Cr.
- Strong order book visibility is cited as a key support for sustaining the growth trajectory.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Q4 EBITDA margin 44.6% driven by operating leverage and favorable mix (higher SaaS/IoT); Full-year FY26 EBITDA margin ~16%; Cost mitigation via value engineering offsetting rising DRAM/NAND prices; Inventory build-up is strategic for demand, not speculative gain.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Cash & equivalents ~INR 600 Cr; Priority 1: Organic growth (IoT hardware, Govt working capital); Priority 2: Strategic small acquisitions; Dividend: Final FY26 dividend INR 3.50/share (175%); Buybacks not explicitly guided but cash position supports flexibility.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The routed sections of the FY2025-26 annual report disclose no named capex project, plant, capacity addition, commissioning or ramp-up timeline for C.E. Info Systems (MapmyIndia) - consistent with an asset-light geospatial software and platform business. The only explicit capex reference is in the BRSR, where the Company reports Nil R&D and Nil capital expenditure invested in specific technologies to improve the environmental and social impacts of products and processes, in both FY 2025-2026 and FY 2024-2025, with the details column marked N.A. The BRSR also notes the Company's view that end-of-life product reclamation guidance on plastics, e-waste and hazardous waste is not relevant to its activities because it is a service provider. On structure, a footnote to the related-party investment disclosure identifies PT Terra Link Technologies as a joint venture in which the Company has made an investment, excluded from the related-party investment ratio; no further detail on its scope, geography or build-out is given in the routed text. Expansion language in the MD&A is directed at the demand environment rather than at the Company's own asset base: government-led capex on infrastructure, logistics and urban transformation; expansion of digital public infrastructure including digital identity, payments and geospatial frameworks; increased Union Budget 2025-26 allocation for the Geospatial Mission and digital infrastructure; expansion of the DIGIPIN digital addressing system; Operation Dronagiri and Mission Mausam; and expansion of aftermarket IoT devices, logistics, e-commerce and fintech ecosystems. Management frames the Map-led business as resilient despite temporary moderation in certain geospatial and mapping projects, supported by Mappls MaaS, PaaS and SaaS offerings, embedded automotive navigation, enterprise location intelligence and government digital transformation initiatives, while describing the IoT-led business as delivering exceptional growth in FY26 - platform and product build-out rather than physical capacity being the stated vector of growth. No delivery-centre, office footprint, headcount capacity or acquisition-driven capacity addition is quantified in the routed text.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident in FY27 recovery citing 'positive inflection point' and 'stronger order pipeline'; Transparent on FY26 misses attributing them strictly to customer-side delays (regulatory/fleet readiness) rather than execution gaps; Emphasized fiscal prudence and clean balance sheet despite rising receivables.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Indigenous digital mapping and navigation built specifically for India's needs, reflected in growing consumer trust and adoption
- Deep-tech positioning with AI-led capabilities embedded across products, platforms and internal processes long before AI became a mainstream theme
- Scale of the Mappls consumer platform — cumulative reach of more than 45 million users after adding over 10 million downloads and pre-installations during the year
- Strong revenue visibility from an executable order book and pipeline exceeding Rs 1,750 crore entering FY2026-27, built on strategic wins across Automotive OEMs, Enterprise, Government, Logistics and Mobility
- Long-standing partnerships with government agencies, public institutions, enterprises and developers reinforcing its position as a trusted partner in India's digital infrastructure journey
- Healthy profitability profile — EBITDA margins of approximately 37% maintained through disciplined cost management and prudent capital allocation
- Full control over the IoT/Gtropy business following buyout of founding stakeholders, enabling greater operational and strategic alignment across the Group
- Founder-led board with promoter executives and a nine-member board of which five are independent directors

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Government payment cycles elongating DSO (Receivables up to INR 176 Cr from INR 133 Cr), though management cites zero bad debt history; Global semiconductor price inflation impacting IoT hardware costs; Execution timing risk on large fixed-price milestones; Macro strain on government finances potentially delaying future tenders.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Reporting segment restructuring planned for FY27 (Auto/Retail, Corporate, Government) to replace confusing A&M/C&E split; Fixed-price contracts now dominate inflows providing better revenue visibility than volume-based models; IoT hardware costs capitalized on balance sheet create temporary asset bloat but drive long-term high-margin recurring revenue streams.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Enter a new phase of accelerated, platform-led growth built on the integration of Gtropy, expansion of Mappls DT and global ambitions through Terra Link.
- Strengthen leadership as India's premier geospatial and location intelligence platform company on a proprietary, full-stack geospatial platform spanning Automotive, Enterprise, Government and IoT verticals.
- Scale a SaaS, PaaS and MaaS business model with multiple recurring revenue streams across software, platforms and IoT solutions.
- Evolve the IoT-led business into a high-margin, recurring revenue business through software-led monetisation …

challenges.body:

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Segment reporting change] From Q1FY27 the company reports market-wise segmental revenue across three customer verticals — Automotive, Enterprise and Government (AEG) — replacing the previously reported A&M and C&E segments, while continuing product-wise Map-led / IoT-led segmental revenue and profitability reporting; FY25 and FY26 history is restated on the new framework.
- [Segment definitions] Automotive covers automotive OEMs (4W/2W/3W and large vehicles across ICE, EV and emerging tech) plus their captive ecosystem and aftermarket; Enterprise covers all private-sector organisations excluding the automotive OEM ecosystem; Government covers all public-sector organisations including Defence, Armed Forces & Police, National Mapping Agencies, Railways and PSUs.
- [Leadership] Rohan Verma appointed Joint Managing Director, subject to shareholder approval, effective 1st July 2026, with responsibility described as including "shaping our Artificial Intelligence roadmap".
- [AI stance] "AI is not new to us. We have been using AI for the last 5+ years to update and enhance our maps"; the company is now "accelerating and increasing our push into AI-native product development, AI-native product offerings and AI-native organizational work".
- [Seasonality] Deck states "Q1 is seasonally weakest quarter for Government business".
